title: Settlement Finality and Irrevocability (Forever-Final Invariant under Public Verifiability)

dascp.note: Formalizes the finality-as-invariant core of C48-N (verifiable that a finalized leg stays final); the cross-network synchronized-timestamp aspect of C48-N is addressed by BPO:0102, not by this property.

iso20022.note: The settlement transaction instruction must reach a final state; the property constrains the lifecycle of a sese.023 instance from pending to final and mandates absorbing semantics.
Status advice must accurately reflect finality once reached and cannot regress; the property's persistence invariant constrains the legal status transitions surfaced via sese.024.
Settlement confirmation corresponds to the FINAL state; the property guarantees the confirmation reflects an irrevocable accountedOutcome.

iof.note: Finality-as-invariant is the safety core of the block — a source transaction, once finalized, stays final and cannot be reorged before downstream action; the harmonised finality-semantics adapters between heterogeneous chains and the cross-chain finality-recognition rules stay out-of-scope as data-harmonisation concerns.

On-chain settlement-finality irrevocability is the technical substrate of legal enforceability — a transfer cannot be reversed at the ledger layer once finalized; the legal-recognition layer (statutes recognising electronic signatures, smart contracts, and ledger records as legally binding; settlement-finality rules under counterparty insolvency) stays out-of-scope as a legal concern.

descriptions.semantic: Once a settlement instruction is committed to a finalized prefix of the ledger — i.e. marked final by the protocol's finality gadget — no subsequent reachable state can reverse the settlement, alter its accounted outcome, or delete the record of its occurrence; and that finality is publicly verifiable from the finalized state alone (a finality proof or certificate is exhibitable to a verifier who trusts only the protocol's finality assumptions).
descriptions.system_theoretic: A persistence invariant on the transition system: the predicate `final(t, s)` is monotone in s — once true at a reachable state, true at every reachable successor. Settlement state under final(t) is frozen: no transition labelled with a reversal, undo, or alteration of t is enabled from any state in which final(t) holds.
descriptions.security: The post-trade backbone. Without irrevocability, every downstream claim — solvency, ownership, custody, asset-servicing entitlement — is conditional on the ledger not changing its mind. Failure modes — a reorg that erases a finalized block, a finality-gadget bug that admits competing finalized prefixes, a contract-level revert path that undoes a logically settled transfer — destroy all reduction of risk that 'final' was meant to deliver. The property is the negation of those failure modes.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Realized at two layers. (1) Protocol-level finality: the consensus protocol's finality gadget marks blocks as finalized after the configured procedure (e.g. justification + finalization in Casper FFG, ⅔ vote in a BFT round, sufficient-depth confirmation under a longest-chain rule with finality bound). (2) Contract-level: a settlement record is only marked final once it has been included in a finalized block AND its on-chain settled-flag has been set; no contract path may clear that flag. Violations live in: protocol-level finality bugs (BPO:0080 territory), contract-level paths that revert the settled-flag, and proof-verification bugs that accept a forged finality certificate.
descriptions.formal_verification: A 1-safety persistence invariant: `∀ s reachable, t . final(t, s) → ∀ s' reachable from s . final(t, s') ∧ accountedOutcome(t, s') = accountedOutcome(t, s)`. Provable by induction over the transition relation: show every transition preserves final(t) and accountedOutcome(t) for any t with final(t) already true. Decidable for a fixed contract; the consensus-level half (no protocol reorg past finality) is delegated to BPO:0080; the proof-of-finality verification half (when finality is evidenced by a ZK or signature-based certificate) is delegated to BPO:0070 / BPO:0074.

formalization.signature: Settlement records t : SettlementID; predicate final : SettlementID × State → Bool; accountedOutcome : SettlementID × State → Outcome (a record of debits, credits, ownership changes); transitions s --[o]--> s'; finalityCert : SettlementID → Cert; verifyCert : Cert → Bool.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Persistence:  ∀ s reachable, s' reachable from s, t . final(t, s) → final(t, s') ∧ accountedOutcome(t, s') = accountedOutcome(t, s).
Public verifiability:  ∀ s, t . final(t, s) → ∃ c . verifyCert(c) = 1 ∧ c attests final(t).
No-bypass:  no transition has effect that contradicts a final settlement's accountedOutcome.

temporal_logic.ltl: G( final(t) → G final(t) )   ∧   G( final(t) → G ¬reverted(t) )   ∧   G( final(t) → ∃ verifiable cert )
temporal_logic.fairness: None required for the persistence half. The composing 'is eventually final' liveness claim does require consensus liveness fairness (BPO:0080) but lives in that property, not here.

hoare.post: final(t, s') ∧ accountedOutcome(t, s') = accountedOutcome(t, s)
outside verifier concludes final(t) under the consensus and crypto assumptions

formalization.state_machine: Per-settlement two-color state: PENDING → FINAL. The FINAL color is absorbing: no transition exits it, and no transition changes the accountedOutcome while in FINAL. The state-transition diagram has no edge from FINAL back to PENDING (or to a competing FINAL with a different outcome).
formalization.type_theoretic: Finality as a non-revocable witness — once issued, it cannot be retracted (an affine-but-persistent token). A settlement reversal would require consuming the finality witness, which is structurally impossible. Provides the type-level discipline behind the runtime invariant.

bindings.note: Direct correspondence: the property's per-settlement identifier `t : SettlementID` plays the same role as ISO 20022's SettlementTransactionIdentification — a unique handle for status / confirmation / cancellation messages.

Partial projection: `accountedOutcome` encompasses debits, credits, and ownership changes per the property's signature; SettlementAmount projects the monetary face of this for cash-bearing legs. Ownership-change components of accountedOutcome correspond to ISO 20022's SettlementQuantity / FinancialInstrument fields, not bound at this granularity.

The predicate `final : SettlementID × State → Bool` selects the SETTLED (terminal, absorbing) value within ISO 20022's TransactionStatus component — i.e. `final(t, s) = TRUE ⟺ TransactionStatus(t, s) = settled`. Binding to the component because individual status codes are not enumerated in the BPO subset of the framework.

relationships.note: Protocol-level finality (no reorg past finalization, no competing finalized prefixes) is the consensus property this rests on; here we lift it to a per-settlement invariant.
For settlements whose finality is evidenced by a ZK validity proof, knowledge-soundness is the precondition for the verifier accepting the certificate as proof of finality.
For settlements whose finality is evidenced by a committee/multisig certificate, signature unforgeability is the precondition for accepting the certificate.
An encumbrance released ON settlement (BPO:0093) is consistent with this property: once final, the encumbrance disposition is itself final.
Conservation-of-value must hold across the PENDING → FINAL transition; once final, accountedOutcome is the fixed component of the value measure for that settlement.

attack_surface.pattern: consensus protocol bug or > threshold adversary causes a finalized block to be replaced
attack_surface.notes: Out-of-scope for the contract layer; delegated to BPO:0080. Marked here so the cross-layer dependency is visible.

attack_surface.pattern: an admin or recovery path can clear the settled-flag for a record marked final, undoing the contract-side finality
attack_surface.notes: Enumerate every write path to the settled-flag and ensure none is enabled while final(t) holds.

attack_surface.pattern: the verifier accepts a forged finality certificate (under-constrained ZK proof, accepted signature with replay, committee-rotation race)
attack_surface.notes: Composes with BPO:0070 (ZK soundness) and BPO:0074 (signature hardness); the verifier wiring is the on-chain side.

attack_surface.pattern: the contract-level settled-flag is set BEFORE the protocol-level finalization is achieved (premature finalization), so a benign protocol reorg invalidates the contract claim
attack_surface.notes: Tie the on-chain settled-flag to evidence of protocol-level finality, not to inclusion alone.

metrics: elapsed time PENDING → FINAL per settlement vs the protocol's expected bound
invariant_checkpoints: no transition takes a FINAL record back to PENDING
no transition alters accountedOutcome(t) while final(t)
every FINAL record is accompanied by a verifiable certificate

strategies.notes: Prove final(t) is preserved by every transition; prove accountedOutcome(t) is preserved while final(t). Contract-layer is SMT-tractable; protocol-layer needs ITP or model-checking against the finality gadget.
Prove the on-chain verifier accepts only certificates that genuinely evidence protocol-level finality.
Off-chain watcher alerts on FINAL → non-FINAL appearance and on premature finalization (contract flag set before protocol finalization).

testability: no test sequence produces a FINAL→PENDING transition
forged finality certificate rejected by verifier
accountedOutcome unchanged by any post-finalization operation

runtime: settled-flag is set-once with no clear path
verifyCert required for every finalization event
finalization tied to evidence of protocol-level finality, not block inclusion alone
static: enumerate every storage path that writes the settled-flag; gate each with !final(t) AND authorized-finalizer
no upgrade can introduce a settled-flag-clearing path
design_patterns: set-once finality flag with immutable accountedOutcome record
finality certificate stored alongside the settlement record for re-verification

assumptions.statement: Consensus reaches finality under the protocol's stated fault and timing assumptions.
Finality certificates (ZK validity proofs or signed committee attestations) are sound; forging an accepting certificate requires breaking the underlying scheme.

No protocol-level reorg primitive exists that bypasses the finality gadget; the consensus protocol's finalized prefix is the boundary at which this property bottoms out. Mechanical verification stops here and protocol-design assurance takes over.

sources: BIS/IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (Settlement Finality)
Casper FFG, Tendermint, HotStuff finality gadgets
provenance.notes: Authored as the formal version of DASCP C48-N's behavioural core (and the underlying R2 risk). The cross-network timestamp-synchronization clause of C48-N is intentionally NOT covered here — that obligation belongs to BPO:0102. The third assumption (no reorg primitive beyond the finality gadget) is the load-bearing accepted-undischarged ledger entry: it names the boundary at which the property bottoms out.
